summary: Ephemeral connection spike triggering GPU attach backoff and mid-window throughput sag in dedicated pool
description:
Issue summary:
Customer NimbleAI reports a mid-day p50/p99 throughput drop in their dedicated pool. Investigations show a burst of short-lived connections from a small tenant group coincided with repeated GPU attach failures and exponential attach backoff from the allocator, leading to effective slot starvation and reduced batched throughput.

Impact:
- Customer-facing endpoints experienced ~30% drop in throughput and p99 increased from 280ms to 1.2s for 20 minutes during the spike window.
- Requests were not returning 5xx but observed long queue times and autoscaler reacted with rapid scale-down/scale-up cycles (oscillation).

Environment:
- Dedicated pool for NimbleAI (reserved GPUs), prod - us-east-1
- Serving runtime v3.8.1, autoscaler v2.4.0, sidecar v1.9.

Timeline (local):
- 2026-03-12 11:46 UTC: Gradual p99 drift begins.
- 2026-03-12 11:52 UTC: Connection spike (short-lived streams) observed from tenant group ID T-9843.
- 2026-03-12 11:53–12:10 UTC: Repeated attach failures surfaced, attach backoff increased to 45s.
- 2026-03-12 12:15 UTC: Autoscaler triggered two shrink/grow cycles.
- 2026-03-12 12:25 UTC: Traffic normalizes after short-term mitigations.

Steps to reproduce (approx):
1) Simulate many short streaming connections (0.5s–2s) with high fanout on a single tenant.
2) Observe allocator logs for repeated "attach_timeout" and increasing backoff intervals.
3) Watch autoscaler metrics for number_of_slots and reconcile loop frequency.

Logs / Metrics observed:
- allocator.log: repeated "gpu_attach_timeout: device busy" entries from 11:52–12:10 UTC.
- autoscaler: scale decisions at 11:54 and 12:11 with immediate opposite decision within 60s.
- serving-runtime: queue_time p50 up 35%, p99 up 4x.
- sidecar: high conn churn metric (connections/sec) spike ~8x baseline.

Temporary mitigations applied by Support:
- Blackholed problematic tenant T-9843 connections at edge for 9 minutes (reduced churn).
- Increased allocator attach retries from 3->6 for the affected pool (mitigated attach backoff tail).
- Pinned NimbleAI to a warmed reservation to avoid cold attach pressure during window.

Current ask / next steps:
- Engineering to review allocator attach backoff policy and identify why short-lived connection bursts lead to backoff amplification.
- Evaluate sidecar connection throttling to prevent single-tenant fanout from saturating attach path.
- Consider autoscaler hysteresis increase to avoid oscillatory shrink/grow from transient churn.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-12 - Jordan Blake: Confirmed attach_timeout spikes in allocator logs aligned to connection-churn window. Hypothesis: allocator serializes attach operations under attach-queue lock causing head-of-line delays.

2026-03-12 - SRE team: Observed that sidecar connection churn correlates with a background job on NimbleAI producing many short inference sessions; created telemetry filter to isolate tenant sessions.
2026-03-13 - Infra Eng: Reproduced with load test harness - many short streams cause attach queue length to grow and trigger exponential backoff in attach code path.
2026-03-13 - Runtime Eng: Noted that attach backoff doubled after third failure; failure often due to device transient busy state from rapid detach/attach churn rather than OOM.
2026-03-14 - Product Ops: Autoscaler thresholds currently sensitive to slot-util changes under 2m windows; suggested increasing stabilization window for dedicated pools by default.
comments: 2026-03-12 12:05 - Maya Patel (Support): 'NimbleAI reports degraded throughput. We've applied temporary blackhole to tenant T-9843. Need eng to look into attach behavior.'
2026-03-12 12:28 - Jordan Blake (SRE): 'Allocator logs attached to linked PR. Early signal points to attach serialization; reproducer in CI added.'
2026-03-13 09:17 - Priya Raman (Runtime Eng): 'Added additional attach retries in a canary for the affected pool. Observed reduced p99 in canary. Will propose code change if stable.'
2026-03-13 16:40 - NimbleAI (Customer): 'Thanks for the quick workaround. We'll investigate our short-lived streaming pattern and provide an ETA on mitigation from our side.'

2026-03-14 10:02 - Jordan Blake (SRE): 'Proposed long-term fixes: 1) introduce attach queue batching; 2) add per-tenant connection throttle knobs; 3) increase autoscaler stabilization window. Seeking priority from eng leads.'
resolution: 2026-03-14 - Short-term resolution: Applied pool-level change to attach retries and enabled connection-churn alerts for customer pools. Customer pinned to warmed reservation for immediate relief.

2026-03-18 - Long-term plan (engineering): Implement attach-queue batching and per-tenant sidecar throttles; adjust autoscaler hysteresis for dedicated pools. Track implementation in GH issue #2481 and Confluence runbook update.
Follow-up: CS to coordinate with NimbleAI regarding workload pattern changes and recommended SDK client-side keepalive/backoff guidance to reduce short-stream fanout.
